claims.statement: Bob Devaney became Nebraska head coach in 1962 and oversaw the 1970 and 1971 national title teams.
Nebraska recognized football national championships for 1970 and 1971.
Tom Osborne succeeded Devaney in 1973 and coached through Nebraska's 1997 season.
Nebraska recognizes national championships from 1994, 1995 and 1997, giving the program five since 1970.

Investigate how scholarship recruiting, walk-on development, strength and conditioning, staff continuity, option offense and defense actually worked; no single factor is pre-certified as the unique cause.
Frank Solich became head coach after Osborne; he finished with a 58-19 record over six seasons.
The 2002 team ended 7-7; Solich was dismissed after Nebraska's 9-3 2003 regular season.
The 2001 team lost 62-36 to Colorado, a frequently cited symbolic rupture, not by itself proof of the entire cause of the program's later decline.
Bill Callahan replaced Solich and installed a West Coast Offense; the Huskers were 5-6 in 2004 and 5-7 in 2007.

Bo Pelini coached from 2008 through 2014 and had at least nine wins in each of his seven seasons, yet never won a conference championship; dismissing the era as equivalent to later losing seasons would be misleading.
Nebraska began Big Ten competition in 2011. Investigate scheduling, recruiting, finances and football adaptation without assuming conference membership alone caused losing.

The Mike Riley and Scott Frost tenures followed the Pelini era and preceded Matt Rhule's hiring for 2023; quantify each era from dated records rather than assign motives or treat them as one administration.
In 2024 Nebraska went 7-6 and beat Boston College 20-15 in the Pinstripe Bowl for its first bowl win since 2015 and first winning season since 2016.
Under Matt Rhule Nebraska finished 5-7 in 2023, 7-6 in 2024, and 7-6 in 2025.
As of October 21, 2026, Nebraska was 5-2, having lost 20-17 to Indiana and 17-14 at Oregon after a 5-0 start; its season was not over.

Nebraska recorded 11 tackles for loss and held Oregon to 242 total yards on October 17, yet lost 17-14. A serious turnaround story should examine both progress and unresolved fourth-quarter execution.

Investigate current roster retention, player development, portal recruiting, NIL/revenue sharing, staffing, facilities and competitiveness. University claims and independent evaluations must be separately attributed.
Washington on October 31 and the subsequent 2026 games and outcomes are not known as of October 21. No forecast is documentary evidence.

interpretationsToInvestigate.question: How did Devaney/Osborne institutionalize recruiting, nutrition/conditioning, walk-ons, staff continuity and Nebraska-wide support? Assess actual evidence and historic inequities with sources.
What changed materially in university leadership, NCAA scholarship rules, national recruiting, competitive balance and offense/defense? Compare competing explanations rather than presupposing one.
Why was a consistent nine-win program considered below expectations? Contrast wins, conference titles, institutional relationships and expectations separately.
Separate verifiable results, staffing and football systems from unsupported claims about personal motives, blame or private conduct.
Differentiate bowl return, defensive improvement, recruiting and roster retention from merely positive institutional messaging; explicitly discuss 2026 close-loss evidence.
